script: Backpropagation's real superpower isn't cleverness. It's speed.
To train a network, you need the slope of the error for every single number in it. This one has 105.
The obvious way: nudge one number a tiny bit, run the network, and see how the error changes.
Two runs per number, to measure the slope both ways. 105 numbers: 210 runs.
Backpropagation: one run forward, one run backward, and all 105 slopes come out at once.
And they're the same slopes. The biggest difference between the two is less than one ten-billionth.
Now a network with a million weights. Nudging needs two million runs. On this computer, that's about 27 hours.
Backpropagation gets every one of those slopes in about 94 milliseconds.
That's why deep learning works at all: each training step gets every slope for the price of about 2 runs.
